extracted.intended_audience: administrative law scholars, agency officials, and policy advocates organizing or evaluating mass comment campaigns in notice-and-comment rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and evaluating mass-comment campaigns in administrative notice-and-comment rulemaking, focusing on when value-focused mass comments should be treated as substantive inputs by agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulates a value preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment expresses a clear value claim (e.g., 'we value X over Y') relevant to tradeoffs the agency is weighing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Campaigns should state explicitly what signers value and the tradeoff being pressed. A clear value claim distinguishes value-laden input from purely technical commentary and makes the normative stake visible to agency decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifies the decision implicated (specific provision or choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment connects the expressed value preference to a specific agency decision (such as rule stringency, exemptions, or methodology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link the value preference to the concrete aspect of the rulemaking at issue (which provision, what level of stringency, what methodological choice). Specificity helps agencies see how the preference bears on a discrete agency judgment rather than as a generic opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrates the scale of the preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign documents its scale through measures such as number of signers, geographic distribution, and demographic breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make campaign scale legible: provide sample sizes, geographic/distributional detail, and demographic information where appropriate. Documentation of scale helps agencies assess how many people hold the stated preference and from what constituencies, enhancing the comment's evidentiary weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connects the value preference to a legitimate statutory purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment shows that the value being promoted is one the statute authorizes the agency to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie value claims to statutory text, the agency's statutory mission, or other authorized aims so the agency can see the comment as relevant to permissible decisionmaking factors. Avoid presenting values that the agency lacks authority to weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allows personalization (template permits individualized input)
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign's comment template should allow signers to add individualized content rather than only submitting an identical form message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable personalization so individual perspectives supplement the mass signal. Personalization increases the informative content of mass campaigns and reduces the risk that agencies treat submissions as mere form letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with separate substantive submissions (factual/analytical content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass-value campaigns should be paired with or accompanied by separate technical, factual, or analytic comments that supply situated knowledge and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass comments supply value preferences; they are most persuasive when coordinated with detailed submissions from experts or stakeholders providing the technical or evidentiary support agencies need for rulemaking choices. Campaign organizers should facilitate or reference these substantive filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign design: make scale and relevance legible (practical design checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical design elements that make a mass-comment campaign count: clear value claim, legible scale (sample sizes/distribution/demographics), connection to statutory authority, personalization, and specification of the decision at stake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the checklist: (1) provide a clear statement of the value claim and tradeoffs; (2) document and present campaign scale; (3) demonstrate how the value maps onto permissible statutory purposes; (4) permit and encourage personalization; (5) identify the precise decision or provision implicated. These design choices increase the likelihood agencies will engage rather than dismiss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting and role of mass comments (not sole determinant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass comments are legitimate inputs but should be treated as one among multiple inputs; technical and analytical comments retain substantive decisionmaking roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should engage with and respond to value-laden mass comments rather than dismissing them as irrelevant, but must also continue to give appropriate weight to technical, analytical, and evidentiary submissions. Mass comments augment democratic legitimacy but do not replace situated expertise.
